title: From Mandi Student to Mayor: Abhishek Awasthi Leads Australia's Greater Bendigo
excerpt: The 43-year-old, who arrived in 2008 to study biotechnology at La Trobe, took the oath on November 9 as Greater Bendigo's first Indian-origin mayor for a one-year term.
body:
• Abhishek Awasthi, who arrived in Australia from Mandi, Himachal Pradesh as a student in 2008, has become the first Indian-origin mayor of Greater Bendigo in Victoria.
  • Awasthi, 43, took the oath on November 9 and began his first day as mayor on November 10; he will serve a one-year term for 2026-27, with former mayor Andrea Metcalf as his deputy.
  • He completed a Master's in Biotechnology and a degree in Bioinformatics at La Trobe University, became an Australian citizen in 2015, and won his council seat in November 2024.
  • His rise took two years: elected from Kennington Ward in 2024, he served as the city's first Indian-origin deputy mayor in 2024-25 before the roles reversed.

Abhishek Awasthi came to Australia from Mandi in Himachal Pradesh in 2008 with a student's visa and a place at La Trobe University. Eighteen years later he has made history as the first Indian-origin mayor of Greater Bendigo, Victoria, according to Connected to India, reporting from India Today's coverage. He took the oath on November 9 and posted from his first morning in the job on November 10, out at Civic Gardens with Deputy Mayor Andrea Metcalf for media engagements.

A one-year term, roles reversed

Awasthi, 43, will serve a one-year term as mayor for 2026-27. Metcalf, a former mayor, is now his deputy — a reversal of 2024-25, when Awasthi served as the city's first Indian-origin deputy mayor under Mayor Metcalf. Under Australian rules the mayor and deputy serve one-year terms while councillors are elected for four years. The CSR Journal reports he was elected unanimously and thanked his fellow councillors and his family on his election.

"He took the oath on November 9 and posted from his first morning in the job on November 10, out at Civic Gardens with Deputy Mayor Andrea Metcalf for media engagements."

From Mandi to the mayor's office

At La Trobe, Awasthi completed a Master's degree in Biotechnology followed by a degree in Bioinformatics, and worked part-time during his studies, The CSR Journal reports. He became an Australian citizen in 2015. He is married to Anima and the couple have a daughter, Agni. His father Surendra Pal, a retired Bhakra Beas Management Board employee, and his mother Champa Sharma, a homemaker, were present at the swearing-in ceremony along with other family members.

A two-year climb in local politics

Awasthi's public career is recent and fast. He contested the council elections in November 2024 and won from Kennington Ward, one of the nine wards of Greater Bendigo City Council, stepping straight into the deputy mayor's role for 2024-25. Two years on, the deputy has the top job. On taking office he expressed gratitude to his fellow councillors and to his parents and relatives, and committed to meeting residents' expectations, The CSR Journal reports.

Greater Bendigo is a regional Victorian city of gold-rush heritage, and its mayoralty rotates annually among councillors — which means Awasthi has one year to make the role his own. His story, from a 2008 student arrival in biotechnology to the mayor's chair, is the version of the migration arc that ends in public service rather than only private success.

His path also says something about how Australian local government works as an entry point. Council seats are won ward by ward, the mayor is chosen from among the councillors, and the term is a single year — so the office rewards exactly what Awasthi's two years show: turning up, ward-level work, and colleagues willing to vote for you twice, first as deputy and then as mayor. For the Indian community in regional Victoria, the result is representation at the top of a city council that did not exist before November 2024, won through the most ordinary route Australian democracy offers.
